title: Recursion Announces $200 Million Oversubscribed Follow-On Offering, Clinical Data Updates, and Partnership Milestone
content: Recursion Announces $200 Million Oversubscribed Follow-On Offering, Clinical Data Updates, and Partnership Milestone October 15, 2026 at 8:22 AM EDT PDF Version Leading Healthcare Investors, includ ing Janus Henderson Investors , Invus , Longaeva Partners , ARK Invest, Driehaus Capital Management and other prominent healthcare specialists and mutual funds invest $200 million in Recursion REC-4881 (MEK1/2 inhibitor) Phase 1b/2 Data Update: Deep, durable polyp burden reductions reproduced in the expanded adult FAP population (18+), with a 47% median reduction after 12 weeks of treatment and 85% of patients maintaining reductions below baseline after 12 weeks off treatment. New upper GI data, addressing the area of greatest unmet medical need in FAP, show a 55% median polyp burden reduction, including two patients with ≥98% polyp burden reduction, and 92% of patients maintaining reductions below baseline after 12 weeks off treatment. Registrational trial initiation targeted for 2H 2027, pending outcome of FDA discussions REC-1245 (RBM39 degrader) Phase 1 Data Update : Encouraging monotherapy activity with 2 confirmed partial responses in endometrial cancer, 1 unconfirmed response in liver cancer, and a 91.7% disease control rate (11/12) at doses ≥45 mg; 45 mg selected for expansion based on acceptable safety profile Partnership Update: Recursion announces Sanofi options potential first-in-class oral small molecule development candidate from their collaboration, designed to achieve a differentiated profile against a challenging dual target implicated in inflammatory disease Expected Cash Runway Extended into 2029, including proceeds from the concurrently announced offering SALT LAKE CITY , Oct. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Recursion (Nasdaq: RXRX), a leading clinical-stage company pioneering AI-enabled drug discovery and development decoding biology to radically improve lives, today announced a $200 million underwritten offering of common stock with leading healthcare and institutional investors, including Janus Henderson Investors , Invus , Longaeva Partners , ARK Invest, Driehaus Capital Management and other prominent healthcare specialists and mutual funds, as well as business and clinical updates across its pipeline, including updated Phase 1b/2 data for REC-4881 in Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP), promising early data in the Phase 1 DAHLIA trial for REC-1245, and a key milestone with Sanofi optioning a potential first-in-class immunology development candidate from their collaboration. “Over the past 18 months, we've fundamentally transformed Recursion with a clear ambition: to repeatedly translate AI-driven discoveries into differentiated medicines for patients. And we're delivering. The proof points are stacking up — with REC-4881, we've demonstrated deep, durable reductions in precancerous polyps, particularly in the upper GI, where the unmet medical need is greatest, in a lifelong disease with no approved pharmacologic therapies. We're also seeing encouraging responses in heavily pretreated cancer patients with REC-1245, alongside continued validation of our platform through global pharma partnerships,” said Najat Khan , Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Recursion. “Importantly, these are independent proof points emerging from the same integrated engine. This financing strengthens our ability to build on that momentum, advance our highest-conviction programs, deliver on upcoming clinical milestones, and build long-term value with focus and discipline.” Updates on our clinical programs are summarized below. REC-4881 (in FAP) Phase 1b/2: Rapid and Durable Treatment Effect Across GI Tract, Polyp Reduction in Upper GI FAP is a genetically defined driver of GI cancer, affecting >50,000 patients in the US and EU5 who face major surgeries and life-long surveillance with no approved therapies, representing a potential $15 billion opportunity, based on Company estimates. Among the approximately 35,000 post-colectomy patients, upper GI disease represents the highest unmet need in FAP, due to risks of bleeding and perforation from polyp removal, high complication rates from surgery, and higher cancer risk. REC-4881, a potential first-in-class oral therapy granted FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations, is designed to address both Wnt/β-catenin initiation and MAPK evolution pathways. The opportunity was identified through unbiased phenotypic screening using Recursion’s AI foundation models, which showed that MEK1/2 inhibition could potentially reverse the cellular effects of APC loss.
